cues.zh: 在足球队里，有守门员、前锋等等。我们可以把它推广到任何基于团队甚至非团队的多人游戏中。如果你在玩魔兽世界（WoW），我们有治疗、坦克和输出。所以角色就是机制模式的一个极佳例子。

cues.en: I don't think there's a good way to build an exhaustive list of this. So for those of you who are happily photographing this, it's far from exhaustive. Game Design Patterns, super useful book. Another one, Advanced Game Mechanics, another super useful book. And these vary dramatically in the ways in which they describe these patterns, but they're just collections of...
cues.zh: 我觉得没办法列出一份详尽的清单。所以对于那些正兴高采烈拍照的人，这远谈不上详尽。《游戏设计模式》，超级有用的书。还有一本是《高级游戏机制》，也是一本超级有用的书。它们描述这些模式的方式大相径庭，但它们都只是一些……

cues.en: mechanics, patterns like this that you can then use. And what you want to do is learn as many as you can because these are the tools on your workbench. So that was the substrate. Now we talk about how you use them. You never, I'll just be blunt, nobody ever comes up with something out of the blue. Life just doesn't work that way. In practice, most creativity is taking a pattern
cues.zh: 机械、这样的模式，你之后就能拿来用。你要做的就是尽可能多学，因为这些是你工作台上的工具。这就是基础。现在我们讲怎么用它们。你永远、我直说吧，没人能凭空想出什么东西。生活不是那样运作的。实际上，大多数创造力就是把一个模式

cues.en: out of its comfy, recognizable context and moving it into a different one. That might seem boring, okay? Just the other night, I was watching How We Got to Now, the new TV series on PBS by Stephen Johnson. There was a glass maker in Venice who wanted to make clear glass. The only reason it happened is because he tried a plant
cues.zh: 从它舒适、熟悉的语境里拿出来，放进另一个语境。这听起来可能挺无聊的，对吧？就在前几天晚上，我在看 Stephen Johnson 在 PBS 的新电视系列片《How We Got to Now》。威尼斯有个玻璃匠想做出透明玻璃。能做到的唯一原因，是他试了一种植物

cues.en: The ashes of a plant he imported from Turkey and mixed it into the glass, and somehow that made it clear. I don't understand why that works, but it did. Somebody else entirely said, you know what? If we then grind these, we could make lenses. And they invented spectacles. But it took a long time to pull that out into a different context and invent microscopes and telescopes. And it took a very long time to pull that into yet another context and invent fiber optics.
cues.zh: 他从土耳其进口的植物的灰，把它混进玻璃里，不知怎么就变透明了。我不懂为什么这能行，但确实行。另一个人完全说，你知道吗？如果我们把这些磨一磨，就能做镜片。然后他们发明了眼镜。但花了很长时间才把它拉到另一个语境，发明出显微镜和望远镜。又花了很长时间才把它拉到另一个语境，发明出光纤。

cues.en: So moving a very simple idea from place to place and context to context and changing it in the process is actually your biggest tool for creativity. And it's the reason why scenes work, disparate groups of people coming together in an environment in order to bounce ideas off of each other. It's why non-homogenous teams tend to be more creative than homogenous teams or teams that have worked together for a very long time.
cues.zh: 所以，把一个很简单的想法从一个地方搬到另一个地方、从一个语境搬到另一个语境，并在过程中改变它，这其实是你创造力最大的工具。这也是场景能奏效的原因——不同群体的人聚在一个环境里，互相碰撞想法。这也是为什么非 homogeneous 团队往往比 homogeneous 团队、或者比长期合作的团队更有创造力。

cues.en: Here's an example of this. You are all familiar with the humble die. And when we use a die, we always think of it in the same way. It generates a random number from one to six. But if you say, here is a die, and I'm not allowed to use it as a random number generator, you remove that from the table. It starts opening up all of these new kinds of contexts. So for example,
cues.zh: 举个例子。大家都熟悉那不起眼的骰子。我们用骰子时，总是以同样的方式去想它。它生成一个一到六的随机数。但如果你说，这是一个骰子，我不允许你把它当作随机数生成器，你把它从桌上拿走。它就开始打开所有这些新的情境。比如，

cues.en: You could use it as a hit point counter. After all, it's got a scale, 1 to 6. You can turn it. You could use it as a timer, right? It's got a scale. It moves up and down. You could use it to indicate state. Maybe 6 means I am knocked down, and 2 means I am, you know, in aggressive mode. You could use it as an indicator of max. So instead of tracking things, it could be this is the max possible I could reach.
cues.zh: 你可以把它用作生命值计数器。毕竟它有个刻度，一到六。你可以转动它。你可以把它用作计时器，对吧？它有个刻度。它上下移动。你可以用它表示状态。也许六表示我被击倒了，二表示我处于攻击模式。你可以把它用作上限的指示器。所以不用追踪事物，它可以是你能达到的最大值。

cues.en: And then, I don't know how many of you have played the wonderful tabletop game Blueprints. You literally use dice as building bricks in that game. The numbers matter, but you're literally building a little building out of dice. I'm sure there are more ways to use dice. The point being, pull a simple tool out of its context, out of its assumptions, and move it into someplace else.
cues.zh: 然后，我不知道你们有多少人玩过那款精彩的桌游《Blueprint》。在那游戏里你真的用骰子当建筑砖块。数字很重要，但你真的是在用骰子搭一座小建筑。我相信还有更多使用骰子的方式。重点是，把一件简单的工具从它的语境中、从它的假设中抽出来，移到别的地方。

cues.en: And suddenly you might get a whole new fresh set of ideas. This is why if you're playing with cards and using cards for a prototyping tool, it's valuable to have a regular kind of deck and an UNO deck. They look so different. One uses colors, the other doesn't, and so on. It pushes you in different directions. Just the fact that UNO has four colors and a regular deck has two, even though mathematically they are basically identical.
cues.zh: 突然之间你可能得到一整套全新的想法。这就是为什么如果你在玩卡牌并用卡牌做原型工具时，拥有一副普通牌和一副 UNO 牌是很有价值的。它们看起来如此不同。一个用颜色，另一个不用，等等。它把你推向不同的方向。就 UNO 有四种颜色而普通牌有两种这一点，尽管在数学上它们基本完全相同。

cues.en: Okay? What else could we use cards for? You're looking at me, sir, so you get picked. Pull cards out of the context. There's a classic example of what people use cards for. Sure. Library of actions. Yep. What's the classic example? House of cards, right? That's radically pulling the card out of context. What's another one? Right? Fortune telling is a classic application for cards. That's right.
cues.zh: 好吧？我们还能用卡片来做什么？这位先生，你在看着我，那就选你了。把卡片从上下文中抽离出来。这里有一个关于人们如何使用卡片的经典例子。当然。动作库。没错。经典例子是什么？纸牌屋，对吧？这就是彻底将卡片脱离上下文。还有什么？对吧？算命是卡片的一个经典应用。没错。

cues.en: Cards could be literally used just for the fact they are a convenient-sized mat to cover stuff up. In fact, let's invent a game right now with that idea. Let's take a card. We lay it face up. I don't know what we got. Let's say it's the Eight of Diamonds. The game is about covering up the diamonds. So every card is now a play field. And now we've got something else that we need to lay down to cover up the diamonds.
cues.zh: 卡片甚至可以仅仅因为它们是一个大小合适的垫子，可以用来盖住东西。事实上，我们现在就凭这个想法发明一个游戏。我们拿一张卡片。把它正面朝上放好。我不知道抽到的是什么。假设是方块八。这个游戏的目标就是盖住那些方块。所以现在每张卡片都是一个游戏场地。现在我们需要放下别的东西来盖住那些方块。

cues.en: Maybe the pips on the card are actually the monsters in that dungeon room, and that's their initial position. Move the element out of its context, and all of a sudden, stuff just starts appearing, completely new possibilities. The simplest way in which people try to effect game design changes and variants and so on is to extend a statistic. Let's add Fireball 6.
cues.zh: 也许卡片上的花色实际上就是地牢房间里的怪物，那是它们的初始位置。把这个元素脱离它原本的上下文，突然之间，各种东西就凭空出现了，带来了全新可能性。人们尝试对游戏设计进行修改、变体等最简单的方法，就是扩展一个属性。我们加上“火球术 6”。

cues.en: This does not work. Not only is it not innovative, it's boring. It's boring because you are not offering the player anything new to learn. You're not offering the player anything new except an incremented number. Odds are an incremented number measured against another incremented number. I use Fireball 6 on a bigger orc XP sack, which actually means my ratio is still one to one.
cues.zh: 这根本行不通。不仅毫无创新，而且很无聊。它无聊是因为你没有给玩家提供任何需要学习的新东西。除了一个递增的数字，你什么也没给玩家。这不过是一个递增的数字去对抗另一个递增的数字罢了。我对一个更大的兽人经验包释放“火球术 6”，这实际上意味着我的比例仍然是一比一。

cues.en: right, or whatever. That's just not interesting. Players see through the patterns, CF, my bulk theory of fun. A new stat, though, completely new statistical metric. That can add a new rule. And if you add a new rule, now you're in the realm of creating a variant. So if you add a time constraint on virtually any game, you might accidentally create a time attack mode.
cues.zh: 对，差不多吧。这其实没什么意思。玩家能看穿这些套路，CF，我那套乐趣的“体量理论”。但如果加一个新统计项，一个全新的统计指标，就可能加一条新规则。而一旦加了新规则，你就进入了“创造变体”的领域。比如你给几乎任何游戏加个时间限制，可能就不小心做出了限时挑战模式。

cues.en: you might accidentally create speed runs. Time was always there probably, but it wasn't a formalized stat, right? You hadn't actually bothered to track it and display it. The minute you track it and display it, goals will be created around it, rules might be created around it. If you track number of moves in virtually anything, let's try number of moves in an FPS. All of a sudden we now have an accuracy meter.
cues.zh: 你可能就不小心做出了竞速玩法。时间可能一直都在，但之前没被正式当成统计项，对吧？你压根没去记录并显示它。可你一旦记录并显示，目标就会围绕它产生，规则也可能围绕它产生。如果你记录几乎任何东西的操作步数，比如试试记录FPS里的操作步数，突然之间我们就有了一个精准度计量。

cues.en: number of shots fired over a number that hit. Let's try it in an RPG. I've actually never seen it in an RPG. Is there such a thing as an efficiency meter in an RPG? There could be, right? And some players would probably find it a pretty interesting game. So adding a new statistic, if it adds a new rule and thereby creates a variant, can be pretty fruitful. Now, you have to watch out.
cues.zh: 命中数除以开火数。试试放到RPG里。我还真没见过RPG里有这个。RPG里有“效率计量”这种东西吗？可以有，对吧？而且有些玩家可能会觉得这游戏挺有意思。所以加一个新统计项，如果它能带来新规则、进而创造变体，就可能很有收获。不过，你得留神。

cues.en: A proliferation of statistics is not necessarily going to be the best thing. And so because of that, I would encourage you, each time you explore adding a statistic, try taking a different one away and see what happens. Not all of them will work, but the permutation of it will probably lead you somewhere interesting. This one here is a classic way of doing this. There have only been five fighting games in history.
cues.zh: 统计项一多，未必就是好事。所以正因如此，我建议你每次尝试加一个统计项时，也试着拿掉另一个，看看会怎样。不是所有都会奏效，但这种排列组合大概率会把你带到有意思的地方。这里的这个就是经典做法。历史上总共只有五款格斗游戏。

cues.en: Everybody always gets really pissed off when I say that, especially because Street Fighter is not on my list. Okay? But if you think about it, the err fighting game is rock, paper, scissors. You've got three attacks, no defenses, and you can't move. That's it. Start adding attacks. That's just extending a statistic. But something like Karate Champ actually added defenses. A new statistic, a new move class, a new rule.
cues.zh: 我每次这么说大家总是特别生气，尤其是因为我的名单里没有《街头霸王》。好吗？但如果你仔细想想，格斗游戏本质上就是石头、剪刀、布。你有三种攻击，没有防御，而且你还不能移动。就是这样。开始增加攻击？那只是在扩展数据。但像《空手道冠军》这样的游戏实际上加入了防御。一个新的数据，一个新的招式类别，一个新的规则。

cues.en: And, of course, they added the statistic of distance. And now all of a sudden you have this game. Most fighting games to this day are still this game. They are rock, paper, scissors moving back and forth on an aligned axis, right? In fact, Virtua Fighter and so on, Street Fighter, they're still this. It doesn't matter if they're in 3D, because the 3D is a narrative thing. It's an optical illusion, right? It's not real. Karateka created a whole new genre.
cues.zh: 当然，他们还加入了距离这个维度。突然之间，你就有了这样一款游戏。直到今天，大多数格斗游戏依然是这种玩法。它们就是在一条对齐的轴线上来回移动的石头、剪刀、布，对吧？事实上，《VR战士》之类的游戏，《街头霸王》，它们依然是这样。它们是不是3D的并不重要，因为3D只是一种叙事手段。这只是一种视觉幻觉，对吧？它不是真实的。《空手道》开创了一个全新的游戏类型。

cues.en: by changing the topology of the dimension, saying, we're going to make that dimension infinite. And it created that side-scrolling beat-em-up, and that's a whole family tree that grew off of it. But it wasn't until Battle Arena to Shindon, which added sidestep, that a true new dimension was added into the fighting genre. And sidestep, frankly, was a pretty lame one. It wasn't an intuitive control. It's still as far as most of the games have gone.
cues.zh: 通过改变维度的拓扑结构，宣布我们要让那个维度变成无限的。它开创了横版过关动作游戏，由此繁衍出了一个庞大的家族树。但直到《斗神传》加入了侧向移步，才真正为格斗游戏加入了一个新维度。坦白说，侧向移步这个设计挺逊的。它并不是一种直观的控制方式。而且这也是大多数游戏目前能做到的极限了。

cues.en: Somebody did actually say, let's extend the dimension one further all the way to a full 2D plane. That was Bushido Blade. It turned out to be a bridge too far. To my knowledge, the last fighting game that did that was Bushido Blade 2. And there it ended. So adding a dimension is an incredibly common way to extend things. If you think about what happened with platformers, this is the technique that was used to extend 2D platforming.
cues.zh: 确实有人提出过，把维度再扩展一维，直接变成完整的二维平面。那就是《武士刀：代号零》。结果证明这步子迈得太大扯到了蛋。据我所知，最后一款这么做的格斗游戏就是《武士刀2》。然后就到此为止了。所以增加维度是扩展事物极其常见的方法。如果你想想平台跳跃游戏的发展，这就是用来扩展2D平台跳跃的技术。

cues.en: First, we had screen bound, then we added the dimension of an infinite scroll, then we added the third dimension, and we got Mario 64. And pretty much there it stayed since then, right?
cues.zh: 首先，我们有了固定屏幕，然后增加了无限滚动的维度，接着我们加入了第三维度，就有了《马里奥64》。基本上从那以后就一直保持这样了，对吧？

cues.en: For those who are trying to be creative and working on these fundamental building blocks I actually strongly urge you to think analog rather than digital and there's a bunch of reasons for this One is that if you step far enough back from digital you realize that it's still turn-based It's just that the turns are on a timer that expires 60 times a second Okay, so you can still apply mechanics these mechanics still work turn-based all the way down at that level
cues.zh: 对于那些试图发挥创造力并致力于这些基础构建模块的人，我其实强烈建议你们去思考模拟而不是数字，这有很多原因。其中一个原因是，如果你从数字技术往后退得足够远，你会发现它其实还是回合制的。只不过这些回合是基于一个每秒钟触发60次的定时器，好吧？所以你仍然可以应用机制，这些机制在那个层面上自下而上依然是回合制的。

cues.en: Right? And so often you can prototype, even action game mechanics digitally. This here is a highly processed photo of my analog game prototyping kit. And this is just a fraction of the crap that I have in there. I go to Michael's and I buy out chunks of the craft aisles. Okay? Incredibly useful. Flat wooden squares, random wooden shapes. Othello, because flipping binary state is super useful.
cues.zh: 对吧？所以你经常可以数字化地原型设计，甚至是动作游戏的机制。这里有一张我的模拟游戏原型工具包的高清处理照片。这只是我在里面塞的一堆破烂的冰山一角。我会去 Michael's 手工艺品店，把一整排手工艺材料都买下来。好吧？超级有用。平整的木方块，各种随机的木质形状。黑白棋，因为翻转二进制状态超级有用。

cues.en: they're the closest thing to a two-sided die that you can get. Random things like stars, chips, hexes, circles, go-beads, a hex mat, you know, all of these things go into the mix. Why do they go into the mix? Because saying something like, could I stick a hex grid underneath a first-person shooter is an interesting way to start mashing up contexts.
cues.zh: 它们是你所能找到的最接近双面骰子的东西。像星星、筹码、六角形、圆圈、围棋子、六角网格垫，你知道的，所有这些东西都混在了一起。为什么要把它们混在一起？因为说出诸如“我能不能在第一人称射击游戏下面塞一个六角网格”这样的话，是开始融合不同语境的一种有趣方式。

cues.en: Working analog, even for digital, is an interesting way to force you to step back and look at something very familiar, your shooter, your platformer, your farming game, your puzzle game, whatever, and make it unfamiliar to you again. And making things that you know very well unfamiliar to you again is a classic creative technique. And it's one of the reasons why the history of creativity is littered with people getting stoned in various ways.
cues.zh: 使用物理实体进行创作，即使是为了制作数字游戏，也是一种有趣的方法，它能迫使你退后一步，审视那些你非常熟悉的东西——你的射击游戏、平台跳跃游戏、农场游戏、解谜游戏等等——并让它们对你而言再次变得陌生。而把那些你非常熟悉的事物变得陌生，正是经典的创意技巧。这也是为什么创意的发展史上到处都是通过各种方式嗨大发了的人的原因。

cues.zh: 游戏设计演讲里，只因为我拥有这个专业的艺术硕士学位。谁能告诉我这首诗奇怪的地方在哪里？每一行都包含字母表中的所有字母。它们是全字母句。完全正确。这就是带着限制进行创作的一个例子。诗歌里到处都是故意给自己设定限制、给自己一个……

cues.en: An extremely limiting box to work in is a time-honored classic creative tool. One of the ways in which artists are trained is that they tell them, here's this gorgeous still life construction of stuff that you should go draw. You have seven seconds, go. And they make you do that over and over again. It's called gestural drawing. And it's done to force you to stop looking at it familiarly.
cues.zh: 在极度受限的框架内工作，是一种历史悠久的经典创意工具。艺术家训练的方法之一就是告诉他们，这里有一个美丽的静物构图，你们去画。给你们七秒钟，开始。然后让你一遍又一遍地做。这叫姿态素描。目的是迫使你不再用熟悉的方式去看它。

cues.en: by imposing a constraint, imposing a time constraint. Think about what you can do imposing constraints. If I'm designing board games, for example, I had a very successful design run with this board game. I took some of the pieces out of that kit and said, I'm going to make a game using only these pieces. And you know what? I got a really good game out of it. Okay? Forcing constraints on yourself is incredibly valuable.
cues.zh: 通过施加限制，施加时间限制。想想你能通过施加限制做到什么。比如我在设计桌游时，有一款桌游的设计过程非常成功。我从那个套件里拿出一些棋子，说我要只用这些棋子做一个游戏。你猜怎么着？我做出了一个非常好的游戏。对吧？给自己施加限制是非常有价值的。

cues.en: Somebody on that side of the room, since I have picked on so many people here, and who isn't Lorelyn, name a game genre. Tactical RPG. Okay, somebody over here, name a constraint. cues.zh: 一个非暴力的战术RPG。这个很棒。真的非常好。你们明白思路了吗？给自己一个不可能的限制，一个让你觉得“这根本没法做”的条件。你猜怎么着？你很可能就会开始想出解决方案。你很可能就会开始发明新的游戏机制。增加一个动词或目标。不过增加目标时要小心。玩家不能同时应付太多目标。非常好的游戏。

cues.en: tend to have more than one goal operating at the moment to moment, okay? Cause damage, not take damage. Great example. Two goals that might be in conflict. That alone made the game
cues.zh: 往往在即时操作中有多个目标同时运作，对吧？造成伤害，同时避免受伤。绝佳的例子。两个可能会相互冲突的目标。一边进攻一边防守。Defender 是如何从一大堆相当无聊的射击游戏中脱颖而出的？就是增加了这个额外的小目标：你必须保护那些小人，对吧？单凭这一点就让这款游戏

cues.en: dramatically deeper, dramatically more interesting. There had been games about just rescuing, and there had been games about just shooting things. Combining the two, Choplifter, another example from the same time period, using the same mix of verbs, radically different games, of course. But you can see the creativity that emerges from throwing in disparate ones. And in particular, they should be ones that are in competition with one another. Ones where you go, oh, crap.
cues.zh: 变得大幅深化，也大幅变得更有趣。以前有纯救援的游戏，也有纯射击的游戏。把两者结合起来，比如同一时期的另一个例子 Choplifter，用了同样一组核心动作，两款游戏当然截然不同。但你可以看到，把不同要素糅合在一起所迸发的创造力。特别是那些彼此存在竞争关系的要素。那些会让你惊呼“哎呀糟糕”的要素。

cues.en: Do I spend my time doing A or B, right? Force the players to have to make that decision moment to moment. Now, your overall game picture might have one of these as paramount, right? In Defender, there's no question that defending is the core goal, right? Because you lose if you don't. But at the moment to moment, defending and killing intertwine and balance each other really regularly. Same thing, speed. We talked about adding the speed statistic.
cues.zh: 我是该花时间做 A 还是做 B 呢，对吧？迫使玩家在每个瞬间都必须做出抉择。现在，在你的宏观游戏设计中，可能某一个目标是至关重要的，对吧？在 Defender 中，防守毫无疑问是核心目标，对吧？因为你不防守就会输。但在即时操作中，防守与消灭敌人非常频繁地交织并相互平衡。速度也是同样的道理。我们之前聊过加入速度属性。

cues.en: Players have added the do it fast goal to any number of games that we didn't think to do it to, which was a failure on our part as designers, perhaps. But today we have the speed run movement, which is enormous, from players imposing a new goal on games that had frankly been exhausted in terms of gameplay. If you add enough goals to something, you eventually add up with a sandbox game.
cues.zh: 玩家把“尽快完成”这个目标带入了无数我们当初根本没想过的游戏中，这或许是我们作为设计师的失误。但如今我们有了极其庞大的速通热潮，这正是玩家把新目标强加到了那些坦白说玩法已被挖掘殆尽的游戏上。如果你给一款游戏添加了足够多的目标，最终就会演变成一款沙盒游戏。

cues.en: It's dangerous to add lots of disparate goals that aren't balancing one another, right? But if you have a multiplayer environment, adding disparate goals per role is actually super critical. It's actually the thing that creates roles. So the goals of a goalie are radically different from the goals of a striker. This one has been incredibly fruitful lately as we've moved to touch, OK?
cues.zh: 添加很多互不相干、彼此不制衡的目标很危险，对吧？但在多人环境里，为每个角色添加不同的目标其实超级关键。正是它造就了角色。守门员的目标和前锋的目标截然不同。最近我们转向触屏，这一点变得格外有成效，对吧？

cues.en: A lot of people like to say the game is the interface. The interface is the game. And that isn't really accurate. And I'll diagram why. But it is a very fruitful way to think about things. How many of you have played soccer physics? Anybody? Go grab it on your mobile device. It's on iOS, I know. It's probably been cloned on Android. Also, you get one button that you can tap or hold.

Changing the number of axes of movement, the time duration of movement, breaking a simple control into a complex one, combining a complex control into a simple one, modifying your inputs. cues.en: Games are, in fact, made out of games. We usually think of a game this way, right? And that isn't necessarily wrong. It is good to think of this is still the game of Defender with different controls. That is a valid and valuable lens. But it's also good to think of the controls are a game, and Defender is a game. And we master them separately.
cues.zh: 游戏实际上是由各种游戏组成的。我们通常是这样看待游戏的，对吧？这也不一定不对。把这个依然看作是换了控制方式的 Defender 游戏也挺好的。这是一种有效且有价值的视角。但把控制方式看作一个游戏，而 Defender 也是一个游戏，同样很好。而且我们是分别掌握它们的。

cues.en: I might be great at Defender on the Atari 2600 or something, where it's one joystick, and suck at the Defender with the up, down, and a reverse button in the arcades. Very easy to fall into that trap. Believe me, I did. Wasted a lot of quarters. Because effectively, there's a whole new game buried in the controls.
cues.zh: 我可能很擅长雅达利2600上的《Defender》，就一个摇杆那种，但一到街机厅里那个带上下和反向按钮的《Defender》就不行了。很容易掉进这个坑。相信我，我就掉进去了。浪费了好多游戏币。因为实际上，操控方式里藏着一整个全新的游戏。

cues.en: It's false to just think of things in terms of, this is what the game is. Games are made out of games, and it's better to think about, how can I take an entire game, chunk of game, sub-game, out of this game and replace it? And inputs are one of the easiest things that you can do that with. Take Defender, put it on a Wii mode. Ah! Whole new game, right? Even if it is still Defender on the other end, right?
cues.zh: 只想着「这游戏就是这样」是不对的。游戏是由游戏组成的，更好的思路是：我怎么才能把一整个游戏、一块游戏、子游戏从这个游戏里拿出来替换掉？而输入是最容易下手的地方之一。拿《Defender》来说，改成Wii模式。啊！全新游戏，对吧？哪怕另一头还是《Defender》，对吧？

cues.en: Swapping out inputs, incredibly useful. Changing topologies, the graph space. We often don't look at games in terms of their graph. I've used this example so many times. Asteroids is not played on a square, it's played on a donut, right? Pac-Man is also played on a donut, or Mobius strip, depending on what level you're on. Snakes and ladders is played in non-Euclidean geometry with wormholes.
cues.zh: 替换输入，极其有用。改变拓扑结构，也就是图空间。我们常常不把游戏看作图。这个例子我用过太多次了。《小行星》不是在方形上玩的，是在甜甜圈上玩的，对吧？《吃豆人》也是在甜甜圈上玩的，或者莫比乌斯带上，取决于你在哪一关。《蛇與梯子》是在带虫洞的非欧几何里玩的。

cues.en: Right? Learn to look at games that way in terms of their graphs, in terms of their topologies, and all of a sudden it opens up new things. In Space Invaders, we move side to side in a bounded way. The enemies wiggle side to side and they move outwards. Change the way in which they move outwards and you get Galaxian. But take that line and wrap it into a circle and you get Tempest or Jairus. Okay?
cues.zh: 对吧？学会从图的角度、从拓扑的角度看游戏，一下子就能打开新东西。在《太空侵略者》里，我们是有限制地左右移动。敌人左右摆动，同时向外推进。改变它们向外推进的方式，就得到了《Galaxian》。但如果把那条线卷成一个圆，就得到了《Tempest》或《Jairus》。懂了吗？

cues.en: All you've done is change the graph topology by linking the ends of the line. You've changed what had been a line into a circle or an infinite loop. And that radically changes things. It really does. The number of variations on Tetris with Tetris played with different shapes is insane. And there are versions of it where the play field has a different topology and versions of it where the pieces use a different topology. You could take virtually any game.
cues.zh: 你只是改变了图的拓扑结构，把线的两端连了起来。你把原本的一条线变成了一个圆或者无限循环。这彻底改变了局面。确实如此。俄罗斯方块用不同形状玩的变体数量多得离谱。有些版本的游戏场地拓扑不同，有些版本的方块拓扑不同。几乎任何游戏你都可以拿来改。

So to really do that that means plants hanging in the air Okay, think about that. That's actually kind of interesting Orchid farming maybe right Plants might grow in any direction. Maybe they spread

So that means they can have arbitrary graph shapes, nodes with arbitrary links.

The steps of the tango, and in fact any given dance, are in fact nodes in arbitrary graphs because every dance has a different pattern of steps. You just invented the dance teaching game. Right? Brand new game. I told you we'd come up with new stuff here. What game is this?

cues.en: Breakout. Space invaders. Yes. Which one is it? Could be either one. It could be both, right? When you take that step of abstracting, you suddenly go, oh, this could be either one. Which means you could do an A meets B. How cool would it be to play space invaders where your method of attack was breakout? And they shot back, right? That game probably exists, actually, because it's almost too obvious.
cues.zh: 打砖块。太空侵略者。没错。到底是哪个？哪个都有可能。也有可能是两个都有，对吧？当你迈出抽象这一步时，你突然会想，哦，这两个都有可能。这意味着你可以搞一个 A 与 B 的结合。玩一个把打砖块作为攻击方式的太空侵略者，会有多酷？而且它们还会还击，对吧？那个游戏其实可能已经存在了，因为这简直太显而易见了。

cues.en: Doing mashups of things that share underlying topologies is actually a really fruitful way to go. There's lots of possibilities there. DDR meets Simon Says, right? That's kind of how DDR was born. That is what DDR is, it's Simon Says with your feet. Try doing this now with things that don't seem like they have anything in common. Could you mash up Blackjack and Robotron? I have no idea! But try.
cues.zh: 把具有底层拓扑结构的事物混搭在一起，其实是一条非常硕果累累的道路。那里有大量的可能性。DDR 遇见西蒙说，对吧？DDR 差不多就是这样诞生的。DDR 就是这么回事，它就是用脚玩的西蒙说。现在试着用那些看起来毫无共同点的事物来做这件事。你能把二十一点和机器人大战混搭起来吗？我不知道！但去试试吧。

cues.en: See what comes out of it. If there's enough there shared in common, it might turn out that, hey, shooting robots and push your luck is a good technique. When we think about a game, we usually reach instinctively for the most straightforward simulation tool. And that might be a really big mistake. Think about it.
cues.zh: 看看能碰撞出什么。如果它们有足够的共同点，结果可能会是，嘿，射击机器人加博运气是个不错的技巧。当我们思考一个游戏时，通常会出于本能地寻找最直接的模拟工具。这可能是一个非常大的错误。想想看。

cues.en: Last year at GDC, I was in Soren Johnson's talk, and he was talking about mostly tabletop game design. He was talking about RTSs. And I was like, could you do an RTS where you don't have a map? Where it's simulated with just cards? That's like probably a whole new genre of game, right? Because you're taking something that's poorly suited for simulating one of the standard elements of RTS.
cues.zh: 去年在 GDC 上，我听了 Soren Johnson 的演讲，他主要谈的是桌面游戏设计。他当时在谈论即时战略游戏。我在想，能不能做一个没有地图的即时战略游戏？只用卡牌来模拟？那可能是一个全新密类的游戏，对吧？因为你拿了一个很不适合用来模拟即时战略游戏标准元素的东西。

cues.en: the real time and the territory, right? But what else could you apply badly suited simulation techniques to? It's not that you're going to end up simulating the same thing, it's that you're going to find different ways to enact the relationships between things. Could you simulate a first person shooter with only dice?
cues.zh: 实时与疆域，对吧？但你还能把这种看似不搭调的模拟技术用在什么地方？关键不在于你最终模拟出的是同一种东西，而在于你能找到不同的方式来呈现事物之间的关系。你能只用骰子来模拟第一人称射击游戏吗？

cues.en: There's probably something there. The die roll maybe is your field of view. Maybe it's actually, you know, you roll the dice in the direction, try to roll it along the table to hit somebody. You start exploring these things by moving things out of their familiar context. Classic example of moving things out of context is by choosing a new metaphor. Now this is not the same thing as just a new skin.
cues.zh: 这里面说不定大有可为。掷骰子也许代表你的视野；或者说，你知道的，你朝某个方向掷出骰子，试着让它沿着桌面滚过去击中某人。把事物脱离原本熟悉的语境，你就能开始探索这些可能性。脱离语境的一个经典例子就是选用一种新的隐喻。这跟单纯换个皮完全不是一回事。

cues.en: A skin is something like Lord of the Rings chess set on top of regular chess set. That's not that interesting. That's a little boring. But what happens if you literally change the metaphor? If we take a first-person shooter and say that it's about cameras, all of a sudden that says, wait, we could have depth of field in the game. We could have rule of threes in the game, right? We could have composition in the game. And we start inventing entire new fields for the game.
cues.zh: 换皮就像是在普通国际象棋的基础上套一套《指环王》的棋子。那没什么意思，有点无聊。但如果你真的改变了隐喻，会发生什么？如果我们把第一人称射击游戏设想成关于相机的游戏，突然间你就会想：等等，游戏里可以引入景深了；可以引入三分构图法则了，对吧？可以引入构图机制了。我们这就开始为游戏开拓出全新的领域。

cues.en: So it's not just skinning. Look what happens when we change this, which is just about visiting nodes on a graph, from eating into painting girders. Painting girders all of a sudden you have to jump, adds a new game, into painting a house, which adds a notion maybe you can paint over, you can repaint, you can have other people competing, which opens up Qbert, which is the same game as Pac-Man.
cues.zh: 所以这绝不仅仅是换皮。看看当我们把这个本质上只是“遍历图中节点”的机制，从“吃豆子”变成“给钢梁刷漆”时会发生什么。变成刷钢梁，突然间你就得跳跃，这就诞生了一款新游戏；再变成“粉刷房屋”，就引入了或许可以覆盖、可以重漆、可以有多人竞争的概念，进而催生了 Qbert——而它本质上和 Pac-Man 是同一款游戏。
